name.text: 15. Lesson 3.5: [DEPLOY: ACTIVE] Output API - Pix & Core Image Assets

questiontext.text:
[SLIDE: Pix Engine Asset Delivery]
[NARRATIVE: Slide Bullet Points: • THE METAPHOR: The Interior Wall Decor. The renderer builds the wall structure, but the pix engine dynamically selects and hangs the correct picture frame depending on the sub-theme. • OOP INITIALIZATION: Resolved via the core output renderer image_url method locator. • COMMON USAGE: Serving cached, responsive interface icons and branding SVGs dynamically across different theme styles. • DEMO PROBLEM: A developer hardcodes a direct path to an image file, causing broken image links when a custom theme overrides the skin. • CODE SOLUTION: Route all image source bindings through the standard core output image_url helper engine. • CORE VALIDATION, ASSIGNMENT & REFERENCES: Inject an SVG icon asset into a custom block namespace header using clean path maps. Reference: lib/outputlib.php.
Voiceover Script: Welcome back to the presentation track. Hardcoding visual assets is an absolute anti-pattern in scalable systems. Moodle’s Pix engine acts as a dynamic art curator. By registering asset calls through the core output image engine instead of raw files paths, the system automatically checks if the active theme provides a custom variation of that graphic, swapping it seamlessly to fit the user's design scheme.]

name.text: 16. Lesson 3.6: [DEPLOY: ACTIVE] Theme API - User Agent & Device Layout Tunnels

questiontext.text:
[SLIDE: Device Detection Layout Routing]
[NARRATIVE: Slide Bullet Points: • THE METAPHOR: The Smart Adaptive Entryway. A building that detects who is walking up and morphs its doors instantly to accommodate a wheelchair, a truck, or a pedestrian. • OOP INITIALIZATION: Evaluated dynamically by the global PAGE object device detection wrappers. • COMMON USAGE: Serving custom lightweight layouts for mobile applications while reserving heavy interfaces for desktop environments. • DEMO PROBLEM: A dense multi-column reporting dashboard breaks layout completely when viewed on standard smartphone screen viewports. • CODE SOLUTION: Establish conditional layout routing blocks inside your theme configuration script based on the device configuration array status. • CORE VALIDATION, ASSIGNMENT & REFERENCES: Set up an explicit design rule that forces an alternate layout template choice when a mobile browser profile is detected. Reference: Theme Layout Styles Guide.
Voiceover Script: The target viewport changes everything about layout delivery. Moodle's theme architecture features built-in device detection tunnels. By setting explicit layout configurations based on the inbound device state, your theme can switch templates entirely under the hood—ensuring tablet, mobile, and desktop users see layouts custom-tailored to their specific screen real estate.]
